title: Albert leads the band; traveling by station wagon or bus
summary: Albert is manager and leader; upcoming jobs include the Fairgrounds and a Pensacola yacht club, and the band travels by station wagon or bus, sharing the driving.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Does Albert lead the band now?

Yes, yeah, he's our manager now. He leads the band. Yeah, he's doing a pretty good job at it. Keeping things going pretty good. Yeah, we've got a few jobs coming up. We're playing Saturday at the Fairgrounds. Which one of the guys was that? Racetrack on? Yes, uh-huh. I met you. It's a night dance. We usually play here in the deer when they have the horse show. Yeah. But this is something going on, some kind of dance going on Saturday night. We're playing from 8 to 12. Oh, yeah. We went to Pensacola Saturday past. We did? Yeah, we played at the Yacht Club. Uh-huh. The Pensacola Yacht Club.
How do you travel now, Brian?

We have a station wagon. Nine passenger, uh, Plymouth. Push Button station wagon. Yeah. Yeah, we've been traveling with that. Well, uh, we have the bus yet. You have a bus that I remember you. We still have the bus. We've got the license for it. We've got the brake tags for it. But he tried to get insurance for each trip. Uh-huh. But they won't give him insurance like that. They say you have to buy it a whole year.

And we figured that'll cost us a little something. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. So, we, we're talking about getting together and get the insurance. Because the bus is more comfortable. Oh, yeah. It's a little slower, but it's more comfortable. Yeah. It could stretch across the seats. After I finish driving, I could stretch across and then I would take it. And when he's tired, I'd take the wheel and he could stretch across the seats and take a good nap. Just about two of you drive, most of the time? Yes, most of the time, two of us, yes. Now, the fellow's been riding with us, uh, been playing with us, Norvin Kimball. Well, he, he takes over quite a few times, you know, when we get tired. He says, well, I'll drive something. Let him drive something, too. Yeah, so, like that, we've been doing all right.
